title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-31
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops / platform notes
Date: 2026-03-04 (last updated)
Owner: Priya Menon

Top priorities:
- Finish capacity plan for Dedicated cluster Q2 (deliverable: numbers + scaling policy). Need final NVSwitch slot counts from hw team.
- Migrate batch inference nodes to driver 535.XX (test on staging first) — see PR #789.
- Investigate spike in OOMs overnight on rtx-pool-3 (suspect kernel/driver mismatch + high KV cache pressure).

Morning triage notes:
- Alert: GPU mem OOMs on rtx-pool-3 between 02:10-02:45. Affected tenants: dedicated-ld1 (2 pods), hosted-api-batch (3 jobs).
  - Actions taken: drained node rtx-3b, restarted kubelet, rebalanced pods to rtx-3a/rtx-4.
  - Next: repro on staging with same batch size and seq len (use replay trace ID: trace-20260304-01).

To-do (short):
- [ ] Run driver upgrade on staging (rtx-staging-*) and run perf suite (latency & throughput)
- [ ] Update autoscaler config: lower scale-down threshold from 15m to 5m for burst jobs (experiment for 48h)
- [ ] Add hotspot dashboard panel for KV cache hit rate per model (console -> metrics -> kv_cache_hit_rate)
- [ ] Follow up with networking on MTU mismatch for private-deployments VPN (#net-ops)
- [ ] Document emergency rollback steps for quantized model runtime (link to runbook)

Notes / hypotheses:
- OOMs coincide with model checkpoints being loaded concurrently; KV cache eviction might not be kicking in fast enough. Consider: asynchronous load with backpressure, or throttling parallel loads per node.
- Staging logs show a flakey nvidia persistence daemon crash prior to OOM. Could be driver 530->535 regression. Need A/B test.

Commands & quick snippets:
- Drain node: kubectl drain rtx-3b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Re-run perf: ./scripts/run_perf.sh --pool rtx-staging --model gpt-medium --seq 2048 --batch 8
- Check GPU usage: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5
- Collect trace: ./infra-tools/collect-trace --id trace-20260304-01 --out /tmp/trace-20260304-01.tgz

Follow-ups / meetings:
- 2026-03-05 10:00 PT - sync with Applied ML (Aiden) on model load pattern changes and cache policy (agenda: load concurrency, warmup).
- 2026-03-05 14:00 PT - call with HW vendor for NVSwitch slot estimate (prep: current utilization sheet + projected Q2 demand)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is eviction policy tuned per model size? Current default may favor frequency over recency which hurts long-context models.
- How aggressive can we be with async model load without blowing tail latency SLO? Need a safe-rate limiter.

Notes to self:
- Keep small rollback window after driver upgrade (10m). If >1% error rate increase, revert.
- Add a quick link section to runbook in the console for oncall (drivers, rollback, drain steps).

Quick logs excerpt (copied):
"OOM killer invoked for process serving-runtime (pid 44321) on rtx-3b; gpu0 free 120MiB, required 432MiB; last alloc at kv_cache_reclaim()"

Draft message to send to #infra-gpu Slack if incident recurs:
"Heads up: seeing repeat OOMs on rtx-pool-3 correlated with concurrent checkpoint load + driver 530->535. We've drained affected node and are running repro in staging. Working w/ hw & networking. Will post updates here. If you see job failures, please tag me (Priya)."

Low-priority / grooming:
- Revisit packing heuristics for dedicated tenants next week — maybe per-tenant soft limits to avoid noisy neighbor.
- Small doc: "How to size KV cache per model" (draft outline in Confluence link above).

End of scratchpad.

-- Priya
